question.text: The Potential Risk Class (PRC) matrix introduced by SEBI for debt mutual fund schemes classifies risk on which two dimensions?

answer.text: Credit risk and interest rate risk (duration)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p78), the Potential Risk Class (PRC) matrix classifies debt schemes on two dimensions: (1) maximum interest rate risk, measured by Macaulay Duration of the scheme, and (2) maximum credit risk, measured by the Credit Risk Value. The framework was made effective from December 1, 2021. Page 282 also discusses debt-fund risk in terms of interest rate risk and credit risk. The Trap: Liquidity and concentration risks, while real for debt funds, are not the two axes of the PRC matrix. Currency risk is relevant only for international funds. The two dimensions tested here are specifically interest rate risk (Macaulay Duration) and credit risk (Credit Risk Value). Note: The PRC matrix gives investors a standardized two-dimensional view of a debt scheme's maximum permissible risk, helping compare schemes on a like-for-like basis.
